This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via getService (symbol, a field of interface HostCryptoProviderContext))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os serve (command, 50 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **37** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b392ff7bdf4c470d422bc8723aa46dc3e301b87a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `476dd4f1d87f0f116be99af44484821020755e1a` — the merge of head `53f848645f8e693216246c2854e079e076e916f4` into base `b392ff7bdf4c470d422bc8723aa46dc3e301b87a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 476dd4f1d87f0f116be99af44484821020755e1a && git checkout 476dd4f1d87f0f116be99af44484821020755e1a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b392ff7bdf4c470d422bc8723aa46dc3e301b87a 53f848645f8e693216246c2854e079e076e916f4 && git checkout -B drift-repro b392ff7bdf4c470d422bc8723aa46dc3e301b87a && git merge --no-ff 53f848645f8e693216246c2854e079e076e916f4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b392ff7bdf4c470d422bc8723aa46dc3e301b87a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b392ff7bdf4c470d422bc8723aa46dc3e301b87a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Request: review · area E2 · head 53f848645f8e693216246c2854e079e076e916f4

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `53f848645f8e693216246c2854e079e076e916f4`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

- **The hand-over now happens where the choice is made.** The host plugin's `kernel:ready` hook calls `resolve()` first, then hands the engine the provider. On the local path, `resolve()` → `local()` is still where a production boot without a stable key throws, so a refused boot hands nothing over, and the unstable-key guard is not moved past. The engine lookup (`data`, then `objectql`, with `setCryptoProvider` feature-detected, tolerating a throwing `getService`) is the same lookup the post-start block makes. After start, the post-start block still runs `confirm()` and only wires an engine the hook missed (`wiredEngine() !== dataEngine`). Nothing is sent unsigned, and a boot with no usable provider still fails closed.
- **Declaration (your question).** `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right; `no` would not be. In the boot window, a `secret` write or resolve goes from refused ("no CryptoProvider is registered") to accepted, and a signed webhook goes from parked/dead to delivered. These are answers an existing caller gets that it did not get before, in the accepting direction. "It restores the intended answer" describes why, not what moved. `patch` is right for a non-protocol widening, and `Metadata-protocol: none` holds. The FROM→TO table is the right shape.
- **Ordering.** Hooks run in registration order, and `run()` mounts the host plugin before the capability resolver, so a resolver-mounted `plugin-webhooks` arms after the hand-over. The real-kernel pin measures that, and the ablation shows the event was parked.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/cli: patch`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Residual 1: an app-composed webhooks plugin.** A `plugin-webhooks` an app lists in its own stack `plugins` is `kernel.use`d in the stack loop, which runs before the host crypto plugin is mounted. Its `kernel:ready` hook would then run first and still park. It recovers through the existing re-arm path after start, as before. Please name it in the PR body next to the verify-harness/cloud residual you already note.
- **Residual 2: a late registration inside the new window.** `confirm()` (a provider registered after init, or replaced) still runs only after start. A boot that `confirm()` will refuse can now seal `secret` writes in the window under the provider it chose first. Such a boot is refused anyway, and those rows are sealed by the provider `resolve()` chose, which a fixed boot that registers in `init()` would not use. Before, the window refused those writes. This is narrow (a misbehaving plugin, and a boot that stops) and does not block. Worth one line in the body.
